title: SL Star Rumesh Tharanga Rises to 3rd in World Rankings
summary: Sri Lanka’s javelin sensation Rumesh Tharanga has stunned the athletics world, rising to third place in the global javelin throw rankings after his monster throw of 92.62m at the Rome Diamond League. With that performance, Tharanga has now amassed 1,324 ranking points, placing him just behind Germany’s Julian Weber and Grenada’s Anderson Peters. Notably, he is the youngest athlete in the world’s top 20, underscoring his rapid rise and extraordinary potential. A Historic Milestone for Sri Lanka Tharanga’s achievement marks a historic milestone for Sri Lankan athletics, as he becomes the highest-ranked male athlete from the nation in world athletics standings. He has also emerged as Asia’s top-ranked javelin thrower, overtaking India’s Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra. The 23-year-old’s record-breaking performance in Rome  not only secured his maiden Diamond League victory but also set a new national record, a meet record, and reaffirmed his position as the world leader this season. Historic Throw in Rome Just days after making his Diamond League debut in Rabat, where he finished second, Tharanga soared past the 90m mark for the first time in Rome. His colossal effort on the second attempt sealed his place in history, making him the 8th best javelin thrower of all time since the introduction of the new javelin specification in 1986. Remarkably, Tharanga now owns the first, second, third, and fifth best throws of 2026, cementing his status as the man to beat this season. He is also the only thrower to surpass 92m since Arshad Nadeem’s gold medal-winning throw at the 2024 Paris Olympics. title: Chamari, Vishmi Power Sri Lanka to Comfortable Win over Pakistan
summary: Skipper Chamari Athapaththu fell just short of what could have been a magnificent century, but her blistering 94 ensured Sri Lanka cruised to a comfortable victory over Pakistan in their ICC Women’s T20 World Cup warm-up match at Derby today. Pakistan, batting first, posted 168 for 8, with Chethana Vimukthi starring for Sri Lanka’s bowling attack by claiming 4 for 31. In reply, Athapaththu and 20 year old Vishmi Gunarathne forged a commanding 159-run opening stand that all but sealed the game. Athapaththu, attempting to reach her century with a six, was dismissed for 94 off 58 balls  an innings decorated with nine fours and five sixes. Gunarathne, who showed intent early in the powerplay with a flurry of boundaries, remained unbeaten on 63 from 50 deliveries, striking four fours and three sixes. Her composed knock perfectly complemented Athapaththu’s fireworks, guiding Sri Lanka to a dominant finish.
